newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Kurdish resistance calls for mobilisation.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish resistance calls for mobilisation.

text.p: The European representative of rebel Kurdish guerrilla fighters called on Friday for Kurdish people and their sympathisers outside the country to prepare for war against Turkish forces attacking northern Iraq.

"Our citizens in the west must respond to the call for mobilisation," Dogan Cudi of the Front for the National Liberation of Kurdistan (FLNK), a wing of the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), told a news conference.
"Our people must be ready, if necessary, for war. They must make their preparations and await the call. They must take their places beside the Kurdish people before it is too late," he said.
Turkish troops, backed by air force jets and helicopters, pushed into southern Kurdistan in the early hours of Wednesday in an operation against PKK camps deep inside Iraq.

The incursion -- the biggest in two years and involving at least 10,000 troops -- was carried out under a "news blackout" with journalists barred from the region and film and mobile telephones confiscated by Iraqi Kurds supporting the attack.
Cudi said the operation would destabilise the region and called on the West and the Arab world to condemn it and to withdraw their support for the Turkish government.
"To stay silent is unthinkable," he said.
He said the attack was indiscriminate, hitting civilians as well as targeting PKK guerrillas, and warned Kurds fighting with the Turkish troops to change sides or pay the consequences.

In the usual war of statistics that accompanies fighting, Cudi rejected Turkish security force statements that more than 130 PKK fighters had so far been killed in the operation, compared with only four soldiers.
He said the guerrillas had suffered no losses, while eight village guards and eight soldiers had been killed and two armoured vehicles destroyed by PKK fighters.
